Local setup, configuration, and report contract

Source availability: The public GitHub repository is currently empty; the project source upload is pending. Once the source is available, download or clone it from GitHub before following these commands.

Use the project folders together: patchproof-ui beside patchproof. Install Node.js 24 or newer. From patchproof-ui, edit the example config with your directly addressable instance endpoints, then run:

./run.sh --config ../patchproof/config.example.json

The script builds the existing classifier and starts a loopback-only dashboard. Open http://127.0.0.1:4173. Keep this local checker private; the hosted demo has no arbitrary URL input.

The supported config uses one approved release for the full expected inventory. Optional application/environment fields label the context:

{
  "application": "Example shop",
  "environment": "Staging",
  "approvedRelease": "v1.4.0",
  "maxAgeMs": 60000,
  "timeoutMs": 3000,
  "intervalMs": 15000,
  "instances": [
    { "id": "api-1", "url": "http://127.0.0.1:4101/release" },
    { "id": "worker-1", "url": "http://127.0.0.1:4102/release" }
  ]
}

Each instance returns JSON. A Node/NestJS endpoint can return { release: deployedRelease, checkedAtMs: Date.now() } when it actually observes its running process:

{ "release": "v1.4.0", "checkedAtMs": 1792886400000 }

The numeric checkedAtMs is the source observation time in Unix milliseconds, produced by the instance—not the monitor’s fetch time. The number above is illustrative, not a current timestamp. Cached observations keep their original timestamps. A successful fetch alone does not make old evidence fresh. Synchronize instance and monitor clocks.

List every expected instance; omitted replies stay Unknown and an empty inventory never confirms. Fresh exact matches count as Match; any other release—including a newer one—is Mismatch. Expired, invalid, future, failed, or missing evidence is Unknown. After a failed check, prior usable evidence is historical, not a successful latest result.

Simulation controls are disabled in configured mode. Checks only read endpoints; PatchProof does not patch or deploy software. This remains one application/environment with one approved release, not a multi-application manager.

Settings and activity are session-only. Browser demo state clears on reload; local settings and check activity live in the Node process and clear on restart. Filters, the auto-check preference, and view-only expiry notices reset on page reload. Edit the config file for durable settings. Activity retains the latest 40 events; external notifications are not connected.

The dashboard checks automatically only while visible with auto-check enabled. The configured interval controls this dashboard’s polling interval. Closing the page stops browser polling; it is not an unattended monitoring service.

Release settings

Every instance must report this exact release with fresh evidence.

A report at or beyond the limit becomes Unknown. Saving settings does not update your servers.

Instance evidence

How verification works

Match means a fresh report shows the approved release.

Mismatch means a fresh report shows a different release—even if it is newer.

Unknown means fresh usable evidence is unavailable: a report may be missing, malformed, expired, have an invalid or future timestamp, or come from a failed check. Evidence details identify the specific reason and next action.

A deployment is confirmed only when the expected inventory is nonempty and every instance matches. In-app alerts only; external notifications not connected.

A match confirms the reported release name using fresh evidence. It is not proof of security, application health, or an independently verified image digest.
